organization.name: Code Tenderloin Inc
organization.former_fiscal_sponsor: Center for New Music San Francisco Inc, EIN 46-1228251
organization.scope: Unrestricted gift to current standalone Code Tenderloin, not unrestricted gift to Center for New Music

identity: Official site EIN and current IRS California EO Business Master File agree. SV2 June 2 2025 grantee update describes becoming independent. June 2025 CHOPP proposed contract still names sponsor; transfer and present contracting split not presumed.
boundary: One unrestricted $100,000 gift. Quantifies only one prospective peer-response component; remaining portfolio/overhead retains all cost with unquantified health. Not observed whole-organization expected value or a current priced funding offer.
mechanism: Direct services include ambassadors/night navigators assisting drug-related emergencies and recovery access. Model additional timely naloxone coverage for a selected unique high-risk cohort for one year, beyond public/partner response. Funding additionality addresses replacement of activity. The residual addressable fraction includes witnessing, engagement, timing and existing naloxone overlap. No extra adherence/witness/partner haircut.
costs: Indicative current official ambassador wage about $27/hour is the only source-derived prospective numerical anchor. Payroll loading, direct nonwage delivery, six worker-hours per unique offered person-year and gift allocation are judgments. Hours include unsuccessful/repeat contacts. Institutional overhead and other portfolio costs remain in unquantified share; do not add a second overhead multiplier. No assumption that sponsored CHOPP staff/capacity transfer to the donor.
clinical: Cause-specific OD and other-death hazards sum. Extra response lowers only OD hazard during first care year. Later arms return to same baseline hazards; integrate finite survival difference once per person, including later recurrent overdose. No recovered lifetime per reported rescue. All hazards, addressable gap, efficacy, utility and finite horizon are analyst judgments with external mechanism checks, not fitted local outcomes.
timing: Cohort selected at service start, 0.25 years after gift; no pre-start health credit. Complete one-year package funded at gift. Ten-year health horizon starts at care start; later services/clinical benefit not extended with future gifts. Constant hazards approximate average risk, not fitted age or recovery transitions.
geography: All modeled health is US; central Bay98% and SF90% are nested resident-share priors, not office or service-location shares. Harms follow the same vector. Never add regional ledgers.
resources: Gift plus unpriced public/partner supply allowance per offered package, including failures and replacements. Gross associated operating resources outside donor cash, not incremental societal cost. Future medical care and family time omitted.
